message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 150, "amount_cents": 12682}, {"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 150, "amount_cents": 12682}, {"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: The handoff says refunds were applied and the reported amounts match the requested batch. I'll check the orders and refunds myself before computing any payouts.
The orders list matches the batch's order IDs and customers. Before computing payouts, I need to confirm the refunds actually exist in the ledger, since the handoff only says they were applied.

The ledger's refunds match the handoff and the batch request exactly: orders 150, 151, and 155 with the same amounts. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 9958 cents, which matches my own check: orders 150 and 153 total 22640, less the 12682 refund on order 150. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 42141 matches my check: orders 151 and 154 total 58011, less the 15870 refund on order 151. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get their net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 50848 matches my check: orders 152 and 155 total 55057, less the 4209 refund on order 155. All three balances are verified, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme for 9958 cents.
Acme's payout of 9958 is recorded. Next is birch, whose verified net balance is 42141 cents.
Cobalt's verified net balance is 50848 cents, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three net balances were verified against the orders and refunds, and all three payouts were recorded successfully. The batch is complete.
